concepts.title: Animal Cell Culture Media and Serum
concepts.definition: Animal cells drink a broth of amino acids, glucose, salts, vitamins, hormones and serum, the fetal bovine kind being favourite; natural media of plasma and embryo extract reproducibility poorly, synthetic formulations run from serum-containing through serum-free and xeno-free to protein-free and chemically defined salt solutions, and serum itself both feeds and fouls - growth factors and adhesion proteins on one side, batch variability, contaminants and purification headaches on the other.
concepts.key_idea: Serum feeds attachment and growth but carries variability and contamination - synthetic serum-free recipes trade convenience for control.
question_patterns: differentiate natural media from artificial synthetic media for animal cell culture
list three advantages and three disadvantages of serum in culture media
why is fetal bovine serum commonly used to support cell growth

which commonly added antibiotics control contamination in culture medium

solution_steps.explain: Natural clots and extracts versus synthetic basal media with defined supplements.
Serum donates growth, attachment and transport factors but varies by batch and risks contamination.
Serum-free, xeno-free, protein-free or chemically defined recipes suit pharmaceutical and selective needs.

worked_examples.q: Which serum is the animal-culture favourite: fetal bovine serum or plant sap?

concepts.title: Phenol Red and Culture Buffering Systems
concepts.definition: Cultures breathe in 37 degree incubators gassed with five to ten percent carbon dioxide at about 300 mOsmol osmolality, their pH held by bicarbonate's Le Chatelier dance or by HEPES in the 7.2-7.4 window; phenol red plays traffic light - yellow below 6.8, bright red at the optimal 7.4, pink above 8.2 - while pyruvate lets cells make their own carbon dioxide.
concepts.key_idea: Measure the pH window phenol red watches, and compare its midpoint with the optimum to see the buffer's job.
question_patterns: phenol red turns yellow below pH 6.8 and pink above 8.2 - compute the span and midpoint of its colour range

what advantages does HEPES buffering hold over the natural bicarbonate system

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the acidic turning point from the alkaline one.
Average the two turning points to locate the middle of the range.

concepts.title: Laminar Hoods and CO2 Incubators
concepts.definition: Aseptic work happens inside laminar flow cabinets where pre-filters and HEPA filtration wash the bench in sterile air - vertical downflow protecting the operator better than horizontal crossflow - while carbon dioxide incubators hold 37 degrees, five to ten percent carbon dioxide and about 95 percent humidity, and an inverted phase-contrast microscope watches morphology, blebbing and early contamination daily.
concepts.key_idea: Filtered airflow guards the culture from you, and the incubator guards it from the world - check both every day.
question_patterns: differentiate vertical from horizontal laminar flow hoods on the basis of operator safety

which signs of cell stress can an inverted phase-contrast microscope reveal

solution_steps.explain: Draw air through pre-filter and HEPA into a positive-pressure vertical flow cabinet.
Maintain temperature, humidity and carbon dioxide levels with bicarbonate-buffered medium.
Check medium colour and cell morphology under the inverted microscope for stress or contamination.

worked_examples.q: Which airflow direction protects the operator better: vertical downflow or horizontal crossflow?

concepts.title: Primary Secondary Finite and Continuous Cell Lines
concepts.definition: Cells taken straight from tissue form primary cultures of mixed, parent-like cells; passaging them builds secondary lines where the fastest growers dominate, and lifespan splits the lineage - finite lines senesce after limited divisions while transformed cells immortalise into continuous lines that grow densely, loosely and even in suspension, as HeLa cells have done since George Gey cultured them from Henrietta Lacks in 1951.
concepts.key_idea: Fresh tissue gives finite, faithful cultures; transformation buys immortality at the price of tumorigenic change.
question_patterns: differentiate primary cell culture from secondary cell culture with respect to how each is obtained
define finite cell lines and explain senescence in passaged normal cells
how do cells of a finite line transform into a continuous cell line
why are continuous cell lines described as immortal and tumorigenic

compare adherent monolayer cultures with suspension cultures giving two examples of each
what is a passage number and what happens to cells crowded at confluence

solution_steps.explain: Disaggregate tissue mechanically or with trypsin and collagenase to seed the primary culture.
Subculturing generates secondary lines of increasing uniformity.
Finite lines stop at senescence; transformed continuous lines divide indefinitely.

worked_examples.q: Cells taken straight from tissue form what cultures: primary or secondary?

concepts.title: Subculture and Cryopreservation of Cells
concepts.definition: Crowded monolayers are split by trypsinising cells off the vessel, centrifuging and reseeding into fresh flasks - each split raising the passage number - while long-term stocks sleep in liquid nitrogen at minus 180 to minus 196 degrees celsius, below minus 130 ice crystals fade, a freezing medium of ninety percent serum with ten percent DMSO or glycerol cushions the cells, slow cooling to minus 80 lets water leave, and thawing rushes back at 37 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Take ten percent of the freezing medium as cryoprotectant, cool slowly, thaw fast.
question_patterns: how is a freezing medium prepared with 90 percent serum and 10 percent DMSO - compute the DMSO in 10 mL

solution_steps.explain: DMSO makes a fixed percent of the freezing medium volume.
Serum fills the remainder of the freezing medium.

concepts.title: Cell Viability by Dye Exclusion and MTT
concepts.definition: Counting the living drives toxicology and drug testing through two assays: dye exclusion lets trypan blue, propidium iodide or 7-AAD slip only into membrane-broken dead cells, and metabolic assays such as MTT ask live mitochondria to reduce a yellow tetrazolium salt into purple formazan whose dissolved colour scales with the number of surviving cells.
concepts.key_idea: Dead cells leak dye in; live cells turn MTT purple - either signal reads out viability.
question_patterns: why do live cells exclude trypan blue while dead cells take it up
describe the chemistry of the MTT assay and the product it forms in live cells
which enzyme activity does the MTT assay report in viable cells
name two dyes used in dye exclusion viability assays besides trypan blue
how are viability assays applied to pesticide and drug evaluation
how is the coloured formazan of the MTT assay measured after dissolution in DMSO

solution_steps.explain: Add exclusion dye; only membrane-compromised dead cells stain.
Offer MTT; mitochondrial dehydrogenases of live cells reduce it to formazan.
Count stained or unstained cells, or read formazan absorbance, to score viability.

worked_examples.q: Which dye enters only membrane-broken dead cells: trypan blue or methylene blue?

concepts.title: Growth Timing of Cultured Animal Cells
concepts.definition: Animal cells divide slowly - eighteen to twenty-four hours per generation - so a culture doubles once a day at best, leaving any stray bacterium to overgrow the flask within a day and making asepsis the difference between a clean line and contamination; population size still follows the doubling rule across days.
concepts.key_idea: Double once per division cycle and divide total hours by hours per division to time any culture's expansion.
concepts.textbook_ref: lebt108.txt chapter opening (18 to 24 hours to divide)
question_patterns: animal cells divide once every 24 hours - how many cells stand after 5 divisions starting from 200 cells

how does a doubling time of 18 to 24 hours shape the schedule of subculturing
why can a small number of bacteria soon outgrow a larger animal cell population

solution_steps.explain: Each division cycle doubles the population.
Multiply divisions by the hours each division takes, then convert to days.

concepts.title: Pharmaceutical Proteins from CHO Cell Culture
concepts.definition: Chinese hamster ovary cells manufacture a pharmacy of human proteins - erythropoietin for anaemia, factors VIII and IX for haemophilia, tissue plasminogen activator for strokes as the first drug ever made in mammalian culture, follicle-stimulating hormone, growth hormone and interleukin-2 - while hybridoma-derived monoclonals from the transplant drug OKT3 to the HER2-blocking trastuzumab treat cancer and autoimmune disease.
concepts.key_idea: One cell line, many medicines - CHO bioreactors and hybridomas now supply clotting factors, hormones and targeted antibodies.
question_patterns: which cell line produces erythropoietin and which disease does recombinant EPO treat
why is tissue plasminogen activator a landmark of mammalian cell culture pharmaceuticals
differentiate the therapeutic uses of factor VIII and factor IX produced in CHO cells
how does OKT3 monoclonal antibody reverse acute transplant rejection
how does trastuzumab act against HER2-positive breast cancer cells
list four pharmaceutical proteins listed for CHO cells with their clinical uses
what advantage does recombinant EPO hold over repeated blood transfusion

solution_steps.explain: EPO for anaemia, factors VIII and IX for haemophilias, tPA for clots, antibodies for cancer and rejection.
CHO cells secrete the glycoproteins; hybridomas secrete the monoclonal antibodies.
EPO boosts red cell production, tPA dissolves fibrin clots, OKT3 silences T cells, trastuzumab blocks HER2 signals.

worked_examples.q: Which cell line manufactures erythropoietin: CHO or HeLa?
